expectations.text: The first line is an action (create/open a specific file or run a command), not preamble or context
expectations.evidence: First line opens with the action itself: "Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in your repo root" (line 1), no preamble before it.

expectations.text: Steps are given as a numbered list of list items, one bounded action each (not numbered headings with paragraphs under them), with at least 2 items and no list longer than 5
expectations.evidence: [script] longest numbered list run=3; longest any-list run=3; numbered headings (not list items)=0

expectations.text: Includes a complete workflow YAML that triggers on pull_request to main, runs go vet and go test, and caches modules (setup-go cache or actions/cache)
expectations.evidence: [script] all of pull_request/main/go vet/go test/cache present

expectations.text: Defines at least one GitHub Actions term (workflow, runner, job, or action) in the same sentence it first appears
expectations.evidence: No clean definition at any term's first appearance. "workflow" first appears in "that's the fixed folder GitHub scans for workflow files" (line 1), which only says where workflow files live, not what a workflow is. "runner" first appears in "Since the runner is discarded after every run" (line 44) with no definition in that sentence (the machine concept was described earlier at line 42 without ever using the word "runner"). "job" never appears in prose (only as the YAML key `jobs:`). "Actions" first appears undefined in "Actions doesn't need separate enabling on a personal repo" (line 37).

expectations.text: Gives a time estimate in concrete units (minutes or hours), not vague phrasing
Ends with exactly one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes, and does not repeat the first line's action if that was the only open action
expectations.evidence: Final line is "Next: paste the YAML above into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`." which restates the first line's own action (create the file and paste the YAML in) rather than a genuinely later step.

expectations.text: [sanity] Contains no forbidden opener: 'Great question', 'Let me', 'I'll', 'Sure', 'Looking at your', 'To answer your question'
expectations.evidence: [script] first line: "Create `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in your repo root (`mkdir -p .github/workflows` first, that's the fixed folder GitHub "

expectations.text: [sanity] Contains no closer such as 'Let me know', 'Hope this helps', 'Happy to', 'Feel free', 'anything else'
expectations.evidence: [script] last line: 'Next: paste the YAML above into `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.'; no closer phrases found

expectations.text: Does not require the reader to guess an untaught fact: every file path and command needed to finish is stated explicitly, including how to create the .github/workflows folders
expectations.evidence: Line 1 gives the explicit command: "mkdir -p .github/workflows" before instructing the reader to create the file, so folder creation is not left to guesswork.

suggestions.assertion: Defines at least one GitHub Actions term (workflow, runner, job, or action) in the same sentence it first appears
suggestions.reason: Wording is ambiguous about whether 'it' means each term's own first appearance, or whichever of the four terms appears earliest overall. The two readings disagree in practice (e.g. a reply can use 'workflow' undefined on line 1 but cleanly define 'runner' via appositive later) - worth clarifying which governs the check.

suggestions.assertion: Ends with exactly one concrete next action the reader can do in under two minutes, and does not repeat the first line's action if that was the only open action
suggestions.reason: All 6 runs in this eval (both arms) fail this assertion - every reply trails into a caveats/limitations paragraph or restates line 1's action instead of landing on a fresh closing action. Worth checking whether the skill is meant to fix this and isn't, or whether the bar is miscalibrated for a task whose honest answer legitimately carries caveats.

eval_feedback.overall: Two of nine assertions show cross-run patterns worth a look: term-definition wording is ambiguous, and the closing-action bar fails uniformly in both arms.
